artifacts.summary: 5-phase plan: close the writer item as a no-op with corrected attribution, promote Check 10's null_value sub-state to FAIL (with a display-cap exemption so the gate is real), update four test fixtures, deploy and gate, and rename task 711's stale project_name.

memory_candidates.content: When promoting ONE sub-state of a multi-sub-state validator check from WARN to FAIL, the promotion is cosmetic unless the newly-FAIL findings are also exempted from the check's output-truncation cap. validate-state.sh Check 10 reports missing_key/null_value/empty_array findings through a single loop capped at the first 10 findings sorted by project_number. With 29 live missing_key findings, a promoted null_value finding at a high project_number would sort past the cap, emit no log_fail line, leave FAILED at 0, and let validation pass despite the exact condition the promotion was meant to block. The general rule: a display cap and an enforcement level are orthogonal concerns, and a check that conflates them silently loses enforcement the moment the populations are unbalanced. Split the emission loop by level -- FAIL findings untruncated, WARN findings capped -- and recompute the 'and N more' arithmetic against the WARN population only so the count stays truthful. Pin it with a fixture whose FAIL finding deliberately sorts past the cap.
